history.summary: The target repair is correct and genuinely evidenced. In playbook-runtime-memory.ts the indexed batch now starts a per-query timer immediately before buildMemoryFreshnessPackInternal and reports the elapsed value through an optional observeQueryElapsed callback, so per-query latency encloses actual pack construction including cache lookup, while readRuntimeMemorySourceDigests and the freshness comparison remain shared work counted only in batch elapsed. playbook-runtime-baseline.ts applies the same shape to the direct path and removes the old post-construction timer that could only ever measure an array index read. The new parameter is optional and the optional call short-circuits argument evaluation when absent, so the no-observer path performs no extra performance.now() and existing callers are behaviourally unchanged. scripts/verify-memory-query-timing.mjs extracts the two real function declarations via the TypeScript AST, transpiles them, and runs them in a vm with a frozen clock; the arithmetic is sound (direct 11+17=28, indexed 5+11+17=33, per-query [11,17]) and the pre-repair code yields [0,0] under that clock, so the RED discrimination is real rather than asserted. Two subtle hazards are handled correctly: node:assert/strict makes deepEqual strict, and Array.from() re-realms the vm array before comparison. The verifier resolves its sources from its own module location, not cwd. Standing wiring is real, not cosmetic: verify-runtime-fact-contract.mjs:82-83 executes it with a bounded 60s child timeout and test:runtime-fact-contract is already inside test:serial-reference, so the regression runs in the standing suite and not only through the new named npm script; runtime-contract.log shows both MEMORY_QUERY_TIMING lines, MEMORY_QUERY_TIMING_GREEN and the contract's terminal PASS. I re-derived every rebound exception line range against the snapshot (new 82/83; EX-1039 64-95; EX-1040 533 and 522-547; EX-1041 732 and 721-746; EX-1042 735 and 724-749; EX-RUNTIME-SNAPSHOT-BINDING 98 and 98-99) and all are correct. Version handling is right for an unreleased Lab head: root stays at the base 0.3.350, no packages/main manifest or CLI brand constant is touched, so no compiled/runtime version mismatch is introduced, and the REPORT correctly defers the bump to finish. No gate is newly at risk: targetStatus depends on indexedWarm.elapsedMs rather than the now-meaningful p50/p95, the report is report-first with authority non_authoritative and gateEvidence false, and after-full.log shows targetStatus=met with equal reference/optimized digests alongside an unchanged M3-M6 smoke. Every figure quoted in REPORT.md matches its committed artifact, and live-intake.json's field set, run ordering, scope string and head all match the committed sampling driver, with live-intake-v1.json genuinely lacking indexRebuildMs as claimed. The decision is fail on unresolved findings rather than on the repair. The blocking one is evidentiary: scripts/lab/u18-static-edges/exceptions.json is a digest-bound review registry whose own binding field demands renewed review on drift, and this commit rewrites roughly forty-five package.json dependency digests, adds a new entry carrying a fresh callDigest and three fresh sourceDigests, and rebinds four entries' line ranges, yet commits no output from the scanner that consumes that registry even though every other change in this Lab carries a log. A wrong digest or a missed stale occurrence there stays silent until someone runs the scanner, and adding an exception entry without showing its consuming verifier green is precisely the allowlist-widening pattern the repository's own triage rule warns against. Five lower-severity findings follow: the new entry over-binds two dependencies copied from its neighbour while leaving its real typescript dependency unbound; sample-memory-intake.mjs introduces spawnSync and execFileSync edges with no entry and the scanner plus its configIndexes 16 configuration are outside the supplied snapshot so coverage is unverifiable; the two new source substring checks are exact-formatting-coupled and redundant with the executable verifier two lines later; the full-smoke before-run provenance commit 3d4aaca544 at 0.3.349 is asserted only in prose with no artifact binding it; and memory-intake-observer.mjs weakens its own fail-loudly discipline by throwing inside a process exit handler and by not asserting needle uniqueness in replaceOnce.

findings.problem: This commit substantially edits a digest-bound static-edge review registry whose own `binding` field states that any drift requires renewed review: roughly forty-five `package.json` dependencyDigests are rewritten from c50dfd8c... to 74981f73..., four entries (EX-1039, EX-1040, EX-1041, EX-1042, EX-RUNTIME-SNAPSHOT-BINDING) have their keys and requiredEvidence line ranges rebound, and a new EX-MEMORY-QUERY-TIMING entry is added with a new callDigest (edfdb648...) and three new sourceDigests. No output of the u18-static-edges scanner that consumes this registry is committed, even though every other change in this Lab ships a log (runtime-contract.log, m3-m6.log, before/after-full.log). The digests and callDigest cannot be recomputed from the supplied snapshot, so the registry's internal consistency is unevidenced: a wrong digest, or one stale c50dfd8c... occurrence left behind in a ~11500-line file, stays silent until someone next runs the scanner. Adding a new exception entry is also an allowlist widening, and committing one without showing the consuming verifier green is the exact pattern the repository's defect-triage rule calls out (the REPLAY_ADMISSION_NONEXECUTING_PATHS case).
findings.fix: Run the u18-static-edges scanner against this head and commit its full output as docs/lab/memory-intake-measurement/u18-static-edges.log, in the same style as the other committed logs. The log must show the registry accepted with zero stale or unmatched entries, so that the ~45 rewritten package.json digests, the four rebound line ranges and the new EX-MEMORY-QUERY-TIMING callDigest/sourceDigests are mechanically confirmed rather than asserted. If the registry supports a regenerate/update mode, state in REPORT.md which mode produced the edit and still commit the subsequent clean verification run.

findings.problem: The new EX-MEMORY-QUERY-TIMING entry declares `scripts/verify-validation-snapshot-binding.mjs` (d62e918c...) and `packages/main/src/core/shared-validation-execution.ts` (fa73cd94...) in its dependencyDigests. Both values are copied verbatim from the adjacent EX-RUNTIME-SNAPSHOT-BINDING entry. Conversely, the verifier's one genuine external dependency is unbound: it imports `typescript` and uses createSourceFile/transpileModule to parse and transpile product source, yet no package.json or lockfile digest is declared, so a TypeScript upgrade that changes transpile output is not caught by this record (other entries in this registry do bind package.json and lockfiles for exactly this reason).
findings.fix: Remove the two copied dependencyDigests entries for scripts/verify-validation-snapshot-binding.mjs and packages/main/src/core/shared-validation-execution.ts, keeping only verify-runtime-fact-contract.mjs, verify-memory-query-timing.mjs, playbook-runtime-baseline.ts and playbook-runtime-memory.ts. If it is, add exceptions entries for the spawnSync and execFileSync call sites in scripts/lab/sample-memory-intake.mjs with accurate key line numbers, kind, reason and dependencyDigests, and include them in the scanner log requested above. findings.problem: Lines 78-81 gate the contract on two exact source substrings: `'overrides.runtimeIndex, observeQueryElapsed'` in playbook-runtime-baseline.ts and `'observeQueryElapsed?.(Math.max(0, performance.now() - started))'` in playbook-runtime-memory.ts. Both are coupled to current formatting, so a behaviour-preserving reformat (line wrapping the three-argument call, or extracting the elapsed expression to a local) fails the runtime fact contract with the message 'Memory benchmark timing boundary must retain its runtime registration and executable regression', pointing a future maintainer at the registration rather than at whitespace. The checks are also redundant: the executable verifier invoked two lines later at 82-83 already proves the timing boundary behaviourally and would fail if either call site regressed, which is strictly stronger than a substring match.

If a source-level binding is still wanted for decoy resistance, match a format-insensitive pattern (for example a regex for `observeQueryElapsed` appearing in both files) rather than an exact expression spelling.

findings.problem: The Real workload measurements section states that before-full.log and before-intake.json were 'captured from main 0.3.349 (`3d4aaca544`)', but no committed artifact binds those two runs to that commit: before-intake.json records only worktree-absolute dist paths under packages/main/dist, and neither before artifact carries a head field. The refreshed eight-call CLI sample is explicitly bound to de2b236e1ae09e21edfe77bc3eaee4cc9725849c via live-intake.json's head field, which shows the Lab knows how to bind a capture, so the omission for the full-smoke before run is an inconsistency. Main has since advanced to the audit base de2b236e at 0.3.350, which the report discloses only for the CLI sample. This is not load-bearing, since the no-regression conclusion rests on the after log's equal reference/optimized digests and targetStatus=met plus the unchanged M3-M6 smoke, and the report explicitly claims no speedup.
findings.fix: Either recapture the before full-smoke run with a committed commit binding (the same head field live-intake.json uses), or soften the prose to state that the before run was taken on main before the repair at an approximately identified commit with no committed binding, and restate explicitly that the no-regression conclusion rests on the after-run parity digests and the M3-M6 smoke rather than on the before/after deltas.

findings.problem: The committed observer weakens its own fail-loudly discipline in two places. First, the MEMORY_INTAKE_OUTPUT requirement is enforced inside `process.on('exit', ...)`; throwing from an exit handler surfaces as a late uncaught exception with a confusing exit code after the measured command has already run to completion, rather than refusing the misuse up front. Second, `replaceOnce` only verifies that the needle is present and then calls String.replace, which substitutes the first occurrence; it does not assert uniqueness. The adjacent fallback-site instrumentation does assert its expected count (`if(i!==4)throw`), so the asymmetry is clear: if future source drift introduces a second occurrence of a needle such as `'if (cached.hit) {'`, the counter is silently attached to the wrong site and the resulting JSON is quietly wrong instead of failing. Relatedly, fallbackSites keys are positional indices assigned in source order by replaceAll, so a reordering of the four sites would silently remap them while REPORT.md's 1-4 semantic mapping became incorrect, and the i!==4 count check would still pass.
findings.fix: Validate process.env.MEMORY_INTAKE_OUTPUT at module load, before registerHooks, so misuse fails immediately with a clear message and no measurement is wasted. Make replaceOnce assert uniqueness (count occurrences and throw MEMORY_OBSERVER_SOURCE_AMBIGUOUS unless exactly one) so silent mis-instrumentation becomes a loud failure like the fallback-site count already is. Key fallbackSites by a stable discriminator derived from each call site rather than by positional index, or assert the per-site surrounding context, so REPORT.md's 1-4 mapping cannot drift out of agreement with the data.

history.summary: The core timing repair is correct and does not relax any gate. runRuntimePackQueries (playbook-runtime-baseline.ts:1412-1436) now encloses each actual pack construction: the non-indexed branch times buildMemoryFreshnessPack per option, and the indexed branch delegates to buildMemoryFreshnessPacksWithRuntimeIndex (playbook-runtime-memory.ts:766-794) through a new optional observeQueryElapsed callback. The shared readRuntimeMemorySourceDigests call correctly stays outside per-query values and inside batch elapsedMs, matching the newly registered memory-query-latency-boundary semantics. Backward compatibility is sound: the third parameter is optional, and because optional-call syntax short-circuits argument evaluation, the existing two-argument production callers make zero additional performance.now() calls and receive identical packs. No gate was weakened - targetStatus still compares batch elapsedMs against targetWarmMs (playbook-runtime-baseline.ts:1487), parityPass and semanticGuard are untouched, and latency.p50Ms/p95Ms (:1520-1523) remain report-only and become more honest rather than looser. The runtime-contract wiring at verify-runtime-fact-contract.mjs:79-80 is an unguarded execFileSync, so a verifier failure aborts the contract fail-closed, consistent with the adjacent verify-pending-performance-reconciliation call. Exception-registry line shifts (75, 79, 527 to 530, 726 to 729, 729 to 732, 92 to 95) are arithmetically consistent with the three inserted lines, and EX-MEMORY-QUERY-TIMING pins its caller, verifier, both read sources and TypeScript package/lock digests; verify-memory-query-timing.mjs genuinely launches no children, so the REVIEWED_READONLY_SOURCE_CONTRACT classification is accurate. The observer needles all match the current playbook-runtime-memory.ts source exactly once, and the REPORT is accurate that resolveRuntimeIndexForPack calls buildRuntimeMemoryIndex before the cache lookup, so a durable cache hit still pays full index construction. Three defects block a pass. The decisive one is that the new regression verifier asserts report.resultDigest against a constant stub (memoryPackResultDigest returns the literal 'unchanged-pack-digest' regardless of input), making that assertion non-discriminating while its printed MEMORY_QUERY_TIMING line is presented as evidence of unchanged pack identity; the same verifier never asserts the pack-to-query alignment that this diff restructured. The other two are a REPORT overclaim about observer output-path validation that the code does not implement, and an unnecessary whole-file re-serialization of the security-relevant static-edge exception allowlist that contradicts the REPORT's narrow-edit claim and introduces literal CJK and emoji bytes whose exposure to the repository prose scanners cannot be verified from the supplied snapshot. Unverifiable dependencies, identified rather than assumed: scripts/verify-proof-or-stop-residue.mjs and the english-artifacts preflight file scope, packages/main/src/core/playbook-runtime-memory-index.ts for the observer fallback-site labels, RED commit 1da2aac95f, and any consumer that indexes RUNTIME_EVIDENCE_FACT_REGISTRY positionally since the new entry was prepended as element zero. The unbumped 0.3.350 version is consistent with the stated Lab-retains-base-version-until-finish boundary and is not treated as a finding.

findings.problem: The digest assertion in the new regression verifier is vacuous. Line 12 stubs `memoryPackResultDigest:()=> 'unchanged-pack-digest'` as a constant that ignores its `packs` argument, and line 13 then asserts `report.resultDigest === 'unchanged-pack-digest'`. That assertion cannot fail for any implementation: it only confirms the stub returns what the test told it to return. The emitted `MEMORY_QUERY_TIMING {..."resultDigest":"unchanged-pack-digest"...}` line is nevertheless committed to runtime-contract.log and reads as mechanical proof that pack identity is unchanged, and the registered runtime fact `memory-query-latency-boundary` (packages/main/src/core/runtime-fact-registry.ts:38) claims exactly that 'Timing observations do not change pack identity'. The verifier also never asserts the pack-to-query alignment that this diff restructured: `runRuntimePackQueries` was changed so the `gold.queries.map` body now only does `builtPacks[index]!` plus `queryId: query.id` (playbook-runtime-baseline.ts:1426-1429), yet the stub packs `{value:1}`/`{value:2}` are never compared against the returned `packs`, so a mis-ordered or mis-indexed build would still pass. Real digest parity is evidenced elsewhere (the million-record smoke's equal reference/optimized digest 19e61cac88d5e038e5114c0059eb7b259ba7e8685c04dc7fdd41ed2c63bf1dc8), but the verifier's own assertion and its published output are non-discriminating.
findings.fix: Make the stub identity-sensitive and assert it: have `memoryPackResultDigest` return a value derived from its argument (for example `packs.map(p=>p.queryId+':'+p.pack.value).join('|')`), and change line 13 to `assert.equal(report.resultDigest,'one:1|two:2')` so a mis-ordered, duplicated or dropped pack fails. Additionally assert the returned pack sequence directly, e.g. `assert.deepEqual(report.packs ?? undefined, undefined)` is not available from the current return shape, so instead capture the digest input: record the argument in the stub (`let seen; memoryPackResultDigest:(p)=>{seen=p; return ...}`) and assert `seen.map(x=>x.queryId)` equals `['one','two']` and `seen.map(x=>x.pack.value)` equals `[1,2]`. If the intent is only to prove the timing boundary, delete the resultDigest assertion rather than leave a tautology, and remove the resultDigest field from the printed MEMORY_QUERY_TIMING line so runtime-contract.log stops implying unverified parity.

findings.problem: docs/lab/memory-intake-measurement/REPORT.md states under 'Static registry and observer follow-up' that 'The observer now validates its output path before loading measured code'. The code does not validate any path: lines 3-4 are `const output=process.env.MEMORY_INTAKE_OUTPUT; if(!output)throw new Error('MEMORY_INTAKE_OUTPUT required');`, which only checks that the environment variable is non-empty. A value naming a nonexistent directory or an unwritable location passes this check, the full million-record smoke then runs to completion, and the only write attempt is `writeFileSync(output, ...)` inside the `process.on('exit')` handler on the last line. Throwing from an exit handler discards every measurement collected and alters the process exit status after roughly fifteen minutes of work. The committed evidence file observer-refusal.log uses the accurate wording ('Missing output variable refused before measured code ran'), so the REPORT is the only artifact making the stronger claim.
findings.fix: Either implement the claimed check or correct the claim. To implement: after the non-empty check, resolve the path and prove writability up front, e.g. `const abs=path.resolve(output); fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(abs),{recursive:true}); fs.writeFileSync(abs,'');` before `registerHooks` is called, and write to `abs` in the exit handler. To correct: change the REPORT sentence to 'The observer refuses a missing MEMORY_INTAKE_OUTPUT variable before loading measured code', matching observer-refusal.log.

findings.problem: The static-edge exception allowlist was re-serialized as a whole file rather than edited narrowly. Roughly thirty entries unrelated to this Lab had their `excerpt` bytes rewritten from `\uXXXX` escapes to literal UTF-8 (for example `packages/main/src/修复.ts` became `packages/main/src/修复.ts`, and `✅`/`🔴`/`─` became ✅/🔴/─), even though their `sourceDigest` values are unchanged. Scanner cache (verify-validation-static-edges.mjs:39-48) stores {text, ast} per repo-relative path and hits only on byte-equal current text; sourceBytes are reread and rehashed per invocation, so digests cannot be laundered. parseStaticSource is a hoisted top-level declaration and the cache is single-root by construction.
